records.verification_notes: Official abstract read via PubMed E-utilities; full text returned 403 (publisher paywall/bot-block). Neuropsychology-focused but explicitly covers psychological tests generally.

records.citation: Abramson, K. (2014). Turning up the lights on gaslighting. Philosophical Perspectives, 28 (Ethics), 1-30.
records.verification_notes: Philosophical/conceptual, not empirical; I read the opening pages, not all 30. PDF obtained from a philevents.org file mirror, not the Wiley version of record (Wiley returned HTTP 402); content matched the published title, author, journal and volume.

records.citation: Akdeniz, B., & Cihan, H. (2024). Gaslighting and interpersonal relationships: Systematic review. Psikiyatride Güncel Yaklaşımlar / Current Approaches in Psychiatry, 16(1), 146-158.
records.verification_notes: The 'no validated scale' statement is made in the Turkish context; a small number of English-language research questionnaires exist (e.g., victim-experience scales) but none is a clinically validated diagnostic instrument. Review journal of moderate profile; findings read from the publisher page summary/abstract.

records.citation: American Psychological Association. Disclosure of test data and test materials: Just the FAQs. APA Science Directorate, Testing and Assessment.
records.verification_notes: Undated web guidance page; content had to be read via a text-rendering proxy (r.jina.ai) because apa.org serves script-only pages, so quoted text reflects the rendered page rather than the raw HTML.

records.citation: Axelrod, R., & Hamilton, W. D. (1981). The Evolution of Cooperation. Science, 211(4489), 1390-1396. doi:10.1126/science.7466396
records.verification_notes: Science.org page returned 403; full text read from the author's official university mirror. Later work (noise-tolerant strategies such as win-stay-lose-shift, zero-determinant strategies) qualifies tit for tat's optimality — the tournament result is robust but 'tit for tat is best' is not a general truth.

records.citation: Barton, R., & Whitehead, J. A. (1969). The gas-light phenomenon. The Lancet, 293(7608), 1258-1260. PMID 4182427.
records.verification_notes: Not consulted directly. Description of its contents comes from secondary sources (Wikipedia, search results), not from the article.

records.citation: Baumrind, D. (1964). Some thoughts on ethics of research: After reading Milgram's "Behavioral Study of Obedience." American Psychologist, 19(6), 421-423.
records.verification_notes: Not opened (APA PsycNet blocked automated access); citation details from Burger (2009), which cites it, and standard bibliographic records. Needs direct verification.

records.citation: Bridges, D., Pitiot, A., MacAskill, M. R., & Peirce, J. W. (2020). The timing mega-study: comparing a range of experiment generators, both lab-based and online. PeerJ, 8, e9414.
records.verification_notes: Abstract only opened (PeerJ full text returned 403); benchmarks are from 2020 and specific browser/OS numbers may have shifted, though the platform-dependence point stands.

records.citation: Brodt, S. E., & Tuchinsky, M. (2000). Working together but in opposition: An examination of the 'good-cop/bad-cop' negotiating team tactic. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 81(2), 155-177.
records.verification_notes: Official abstract read via NLM EFetch (PMID 10706812); full text paywalled. Vignette studies of a hypothetical workgroup, not live negotiations. Per the recognition-only brief, effectiveness-optimizing details (e.g., role ordering) were deliberately not extracted.

records.citation: Burger, J. M. (2009). Replicating Milgram: Would people still obey today? American Psychologist, 64(1), 1-11.
records.verification_notes: Single partial replication, one US site; heavy screening of vulnerable people and the hard stop at 150 volts mean the 70% figure is an estimate of willingness, not observed continuation to 450 volts. Pages 1-8 read (including the results tables); final pages 9-11 not read.

records.citation: Cohen, J. D., Dunbar, K., & McClelland, J. L. (1990). On the control of automatic processes: A parallel distributed processing account of the Stroop effect. Psychological Review, 97(3), 332-361.
records.verification_notes: Abstract only opened (full text paywalled at APA); it is one model among several competitors, so it supports the 'strength/practice' framing but not a settled mechanism.

records.citation: Cosmides, L. (1989). The logic of social exchange: Has natural selection shaped how humans reason? Studies with the Wason selection task. Cognition, 31(3), 187–276.
records.verification_notes: Paywalled; abstract could not be read directly, so specific within-paper results are not asserted from it. Bibliographic details verified via DOI metadata.

records.verification_notes: Authored by the originators of social contract theory, defending it against critics; the performance figures are robust but the evolved-module interpretation is contested (see the contested-mechanism claim).

records.verification_notes: Abstract-level access only; full text is behind the Sage paywall, so page-level quotations come via secondary citation in Devine (2021).

records.verification_notes: Abstract only (Wiley full text returned HTTP 402 despite hybrid OA flag). Small, self-selected, retrospective sample of people who already identified as survivors; cannot establish prevalence or causation.

records.verification_notes: Full text paywalled; only the official abstract was opened, so exact condition percentages were taken from a secondary peer-reviewed report (Tubau et al. 2015).

records.citation: Liberman, V., Samuels, S. M., & Ross, L. (2004). The Name of the Game: Predictive Power of Reputations versus Situational Labels in Determining Prisoner's Dilemma Game Moves. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 30(9), 1175-1185. doi:10.1177/0146167204264004
records.verification_notes: Abstract only (full text paywalled); widely quoted exact percentages (roughly 70% vs 33% first-round cooperation by label) come from secondary sources and were not verified in the opened abstract, so the claim text avoids precise numbers. Anchored on one two-experiment paper, though it converges with the broader framing literature and with Mengel's finding that payoff parameters drive most variation.

records.verification_notes: Abstract-level access via PubMed E-utilities; predates the 2013 meta-analyses and R-PAS. Part of the same critique tradition as the 'What's Wrong with the Rorschach' debate (Wood et al., 2003 book, not opened).

records.verification_notes: Backlash measured as within-experiment dropout and self-reported frustration in one study; real-world reputational consequences were not directly measured.

records.citation: Luguri, J., & Strahilevitz, L. J. (2021). Shining a Light on Dark Patterns. Journal of Legal Analysis, 13(1), 43–109. DOI: 10.1093/jla/laaa006.
records.verification_notes: Two experiments by one team, US online sample, one product context (identity-theft protection); percentages are context-specific and should not be read as universal effect sizes.

records.citation: MacLeod, C. M. (1991). Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review. Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163-203.
records.verification_notes: Narrative review, not a quantitative meta-analysis; opened via a third-party PDF mirror (wexler.free.fr), content matches the APA-published pagination.

records.citation: MacLeod, C. M. (2015). The Stroop effect. In Encyclopedia of Color Science and Technology. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-642-27851-8_67-1
records.verification_notes: Tertiary/encyclopedia source, though written by the field's leading reviewer; also notes automaticity alone is not the settled full explanation.

records.verification_notes: Covers studies from roughly 1997-2007 only; the authors themselves report substantial heterogeneity, possible publication bias, small samples for some comparisons, and results that cannot be generalized beyond the anxiety dimension.

records.verification_notes: Abstract and project page read; full paper PDF not opened. Automated detection focused on text-based patterns on shopping sites, so the count is a lower bound and does not cover purely visual patterns or non-shopping contexts.

records.citation: Ragni, M., Kola, I., & Johnson-Laird, P. N. (2017). The Wason Selection Task: A Meta-Analysis. Proceedings of the 39th Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society, 980–985.
records.verification_notes: Meta-analytic averages pool heterogeneous materials and populations; 'about two-thirds' is the pooled canonical-selection percentage, not a universal constant.

records.citation: Ragni, M., Kola, I., & Johnson-Laird, P. N. (2017). The Wason Selection Task: A Meta-Analysis. Proceedings of the 39th Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society, 980–985.
